key_provisions_or_claims: Social robots can act as agents or fulcrums of cultural transmission, especially for children.
Roboethics guidelines raise the question of whose values and vision of the ideal society inform policy.
Roboethics risks becoming an instrument of political social engineering without consensus on a better society.
The engineering field's 'technological imagination' biases ethical appraisals toward risk minimisation and tunnel vision.
Heeds C. Wright Mills' 'cheerful robot' metaphor as a warning about passive acceptance and technological determinism.
annotation.summary_en: Conceptual paper on meta-ethical issues of socially interactive robots, organised as questions on cultural transmission, social engineering in roboethics, technological imagination and determinism. It questions whose values shape robot ethics policy and invokes C. Wright Mills' 'cheerful robot' metaphor, without proposing concrete regulation.
annotation.title_clean: Engineering Cheerful Robots: An Ethical Consideration
annotation.title_en: Engineering Cheerful Robots: An Ethical Consideration
